Photograph: Jewel Samad/AFP/Getty Images Cyprus Nearly 20 people still missing after ferry capsizes ⁠off northern Cyprus Divers join search teams scouring deep waters for ⁠any survivors, with eight people so far confirmed to have died Reuters in Nicosia Mon 31 Aug 2026 05.49 EDT Last modified on Mon 31 Aug 2026 05.53 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Nearly 20 people are still missing after a ferry capsized ⁠off northern Cyprus , killing at least eight, as divers join search teams scouring deep waters for ⁠any survivors. The double-hulled ⁠ferry ​with 267 people onboard took in water and flipped over on Sunday just off the port city ⁠of Kyrenia, leaving survivors clinging to the upturned hull. They were rescued by passing vessels and members of the coastguard. “We’ve been waiting since the morning, for 12 hours or ​maybe more,” said Naif Ezer, ‌one of those ‌waiting anxiously outside the port for news of passengers through the ‌early hours of Monday. Of three friends travelling home to see their families, one had been found but the other two were still missing, he added. Some of those waiting sat and wept, while others scrolled mobile phones for updates. View image in fullscreen Passengers being rescued from the capsized ferry on Sunday. Photograph: Reuters TV/Reuters It was unclear ‌if people remained trapped on the vessel, now lying on the seabed at a depth of more ​than 500 metres (1,640ft). Divers from Turkey were assisting the search, officials said. They gave differing estimates of the number of missing, with some saying 19 and others 18. The ferry ran into trouble shortly ⁠after leaving Kyrenia for the Turkish port of Taşucu in ​Mersin province, ​one of several daily sea shuttle ​links between Turkish-occupied northern Cyprus and mainland Turkey. Separate accounts said the wide-bodied ​vessel jolted violently before ‌slamming on to ​the sea ​surface, with part of its bow bursting open on impact. Authorities have detained the captain and crew of the vessel for questioning. http://www.euronews.com/2026/09/01/exclu.text: UN Secretary-General António Guterres has urged world leaders gathered in Bishkek to "stop the madness" and end the world's wars.Speaking to Euronews in the Kyrgyz capital on the margins of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit on Tuesday, the UN chief said the meeting was a rare chance to put the case directly to the people who could act on it."A very important message is to say, it is time to stop this madness. It is time for peace. And some of the key actors of these processes are here," Guterres said."What worries us more is the fact that we have conflicts that seem never-ending. It is true in relation to Russia and Ukraine. It is true in relation to the Middle East, both from Gaza to the Iran and United States confrontation," he added.'We need to go back to where we were'On Iran, Guterres said strikes had resumed, and called for both sides to return to negotiations, which he said had come close to succeeding."Unfortunately, the strikes have started again. So I think maximum containment is necessary," he said."We need to go back to where we were. There were negotiations that seemed to be successful," Guterres pointed out."Let's restart them, and let's make sure that we create a situation of peace and stability in the area, and especially that the freedom of navigation is fully re-established, both in the Strait of Hormuz and in Bab el-Mandeb."Guterres, who attends the SCO as a guest, said engaging with regional organisations has become central to how the UN works."We live more and more in a multipolar world. And obviously, for an organisation like the UN, it is extremely important to engage with regional organisations, be it the European Union, the African Union, or the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation," he told Euronews.The bloc is marking its 25th anniversary in Bishkek. Its 10 members are China, Russia, India, Pakistan, Iran, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan, and between them they account for more than 40% of the world's population.A further 15 states attend as dialogue partners, among them Turkey, whose President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan is in Bishkek alongside Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian."Here you have a platform, in which practically half of humanity is represented. And the most dynamic economies in the world are today in Asia," Guterres said."So for me as secretary-general, it's very important to maintain a dialogue with the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation and to cooperate with them in the areas that are areas of common interest," the UN chief concluded.The one-day summit closes in Bishkek on Tuesday.
